title: Air Premia says call-centre contractor MetaM was hacked; customer data and call recordings may have been exposed, Dailysecu reports
date_note: Dailysecu says Air Premia posted its notice on its website on 26 November.
geo_basis: The article names no city; the pin is a general location in South Korea.
summary: Dailysecu reports that MetaM, the contractor handling Air Premia's customer consultations, was hacked, and customer names, phone numbers, consultation records and call recordings may have been exposed. According to MetaM, unauthorized access is presumed to have begun on 4 November and MetaM noticed it on 12 November. Dailysecu says no actual external leak has been confirmed and investigations are under way.
plain: Air Premia's call-centre contractor was hacked, and customer names, phone numbers, consultation records and call recordings may have been exposed. No actual leak has been confirmed, Dailysecu says.
exec: A contractor's breach may have exposed Air Premia customers' call data; Dailysecu says no external leak has been confirmed yet.
action: Air Premia urges customers to be wary of impersonation calls, texts and emails citing ticket changes, refunds or compensation, Dailysecu reports.

validation.note: Only Dailysecu was read, relaying Air Premia's website notice; the notice itself was not found.

review.note: Compared title, 26 Nov notice, 4/12 Nov dates, possible exposure, no confirmed leak, advice against Dailysecu
